question: What does incidence measure in a target population?

options.D: Total existing cases of a disease

explanation: Incidence tracks newly diagnosed cases over a set period to show how fast a condition spreads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h1)

question: Why must the denominator in an incidence calculation exclude people who already have the condition?

options.A: Only people at risk of getting the disease should be counted
options.B: It simplifies mathematical calculations for community health workers
options.C: Existing cases are automatically added to the numerator instead
options.D: Patients with the disease no longer live in the community

explanation: The population at risk must only include disease-free individuals capable of developing the new condition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h1)

question: Prevalence differs from incidence because prevalence measures which of the following?

options.A: All existing cases at a specific time
options.B: The rate of recovery from an infection
options.C: Total deaths caused by an outbreak
options.D: Only newly diagnosed cases in a year

explanation: Prevalence captures the total burden by counting both old and existing cases together at one moment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h2)

question: A community clinic plans resource allocation for long-term care of diabetic patients. Which metric is most useful?
explanation: Prevalence shows the total number of people living with a condition, helping plan ongoing care and drug supplies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h2)

question: What value is multiplied by the fraction to express incidence per standard population size?

options.A: The average age of the affected patients
options.C: The total number of hospital beds available
options.D: The total number of recovered individuals

explanation: Multiplying by a factor like 1,000 or 100,000 standardizes the figure for clear reporting and comparison. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h3)

question: What happens to the incidence rate if individuals in the denominator already have the disease?

options.B: The time factor is automatically doubled

explanation: Including immune or already-sick people in the denominator wrongly increases the population at risk, deflating the rate. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h3)

question: Cumulative incidence assumes that every person in the study group is followed for what duration?

options.B: Until they migrate out of the country
options.C: Until they develop a secondary illness
options.D: Only the first few days of life

explanation: Cumulative incidence requires complete follow-up of all participants across the full duration of observation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h4)

question: When is incidence density preferred over cumulative incidence in public health research?

options.A: When studying non-infectious chronic conditions exclusively
options.B: When the researcher wants to measure total existing cases
options.C: When study participants enter or leave at different times
options.D: When every single patient stays in the study until the end

explanation: Incidence density uses person-time denominators to handle loss to follow-up or migration in dynamic populations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h4)

question: Which factor directly drives down the incidence of vaccine-preventable diseases in a community?
explanation: Immunization builds community immunity, preventing susceptible individuals from contracting and spreading infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h5)

question: Why does increased seasonal rainfall often lead to a spike in malaria incidence in Nigeria?

options.A: It lowers the nutritional status of rural farmers
options.B: It forces people to crowd into closed indoor spaces
options.C: It washes away essential community medication stocks
options.D: It creates breeding sites for mosquito vectors

explanation: Standing water pools from heavy rains provide ideal environments for mosquitoes to multiply and transmit malaria. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h5)

question: What is the primary public health purpose of monitoring weekly disease incidence?

options.A: Detecting outbreaks early to trigger rapid responses

explanation: Monitoring new cases week by week allows health teams to spot unusual clustering and stop outbreaks early. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h6)

question: How do public health nurses use incidence trends over several years?

options.A: To set pharmaceutical drug prices in local markets
options.B: To evaluate the success of disease control programs
options.C: To diagnose individual patients reporting to the clinic
options.D: To determine daily staff shift rosters in the ward

explanation: Comparing yearly incidence curves shows whether public health interventions are successfully reducing disease transmission. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h6)

question: Which Nigerian health workers are frontline reporters for new disease cases in communities?

options.B: Nurses and community health extension workers

explanation: Nurses and CHEWs staff primary health centres and spot new cases during routine patient consultations. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h7)

question: A primary health centre in a rural Nigerian LGA notes a sudden rise in suspected cholera cases. What immediate action should follow?

options.A: Transfer all health personnel to urban tertiary hospitals
options.B: Report the incidence data upward to trigger rapid response teams
options.C: Stop recording patient visits to reduce administrative workload
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to publish a formal report

explanation: Prompt reporting of new cases ensures higher health authorities deploy aid and containment measures immediately. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h7)
